blocks.vo_line: On August 28th, the Moon turns to shadow. Don't miss it.
This is the Corn Moon. The final one before autumn. But this year, it doesn't just rise.
It gets partially eaten. Earth slides between the Sun and the Moon,
and a dark bite carves into the surface, right in front of you. No telescope. Nothing to set up. Just look up.
Two weeks ago the Moon blocked the Sun. Now the Earth returns the favor.
It peaks after moonrise — visible across the Americas, Europe, and Africa. And then it's gone.
So here's my question. When it happens, are you actually going outside to watch? Or will you forget, scroll past this, and see the photos tomorrow wishing you'd looked?
Tell me below. I'm reading every single one.
